truths.truth: A Cadence dispatch whose hand-written close never runs is still closed by the host's SubagentStop hook
truths.evidence: Registration and script are real and correct: hooks/hooks.json:27-37 declares SubagentStop -> node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/cadence-core/bin/subagent-trace.mjs", no matcher, timeout 10. Driven end to end against a scratch project (/tmp scratchpad/p2) with one open cad-executor dispatch and NO hand-written close: piping {cwd, agent_type:'cadence:cad-executor-xhigh'} into cadence-core/bin/subagent-trace.mjs printed nothing, exited 0, appended one lifecycle/return quoting the dispatch's own corr 9-aaaa/phase/plan, and `trace render` then showed brackets:1, unpaired:[]. The payload shape is the host's own: the 2.1.245 binary's zod schema reads hook_event_name:'SubagentStop', stop_hook_active, agent_id, agent_transcript_path, agent_type - no corr, phase, tokens or duration, which is D-01 confirmed independently. What no probe here can settle is the host actually invoking the registered hook in a live session.

truths.truth: A dispatch closed only from the host side is listed under brackets, not unpaired, so a bracket outlives the session that opened it
truths.evidence: Same scratch run as truth 2: before the pipe, `trace render` listed the dispatch under unpaired ([{corr:'9-aaaa',phase:'2',plan:'1',ts:...,role:'cad-executor'}]) and brackets was empty; after the hook alone wrote its close, brackets held that row and unpaired was []. The hook adopts rather than derives - cadence-core/bin/lib/subagent-trace.mjs:93-127 reads render.unpaired, keeps the newest row of the mapped role and quotes its corr/phase/plan - and appendEvent honours the caller's corr, which is what made the pairing hold. Only the live half is unproven: no bracket on .planning/trace.jsonl was written by the host (the hook was registered mid-run, so this phase's own two closes came from the hand-written path).

truths.truth: Two writers closing one dispatch render as exactly one bracket in either arrival order, with no second unpaired row and no double billing
truths.evidence: The dedup is real code, not the old replay guard: cadence-core/bin/lib/trace.mjs:641-664 keeps seenTerminals (which keys on the millisecond and cannot fold two writers) and adds pairedRows, a (corr,phase,plan) map; :770-772 registers the row a pairing owns and :825-840 folds a repeat close into it, filling only empty fields and upgrading `return`->`checkpoint` one direction only. Driven with the two REAL writers against scratch fixtures: hook first then `trace close --tokens 12345 --turns 7 --duration-ms '1m 23s' --detail ...`, and the same pair reversed, both render {brackets:1, unpaired:[], roles:{cad-executor:{dispatches:1,tokens:12345,turns:9->7}}} with event 'checkpoint' and duration_ms 83000 surviving in both orders. Named tests: cadence-core/bin/trace.test.mjs:1640-1687 ('a dispatch closed by BOTH writers is exactly one bracket' asserting brackets.length===1, 'the two closes render identically in EITHER arrival order', 'two genuine dispatches on ONE worker key are still two brackets').

human_checks.name: SubagentStop registered and closes a dispatch with no hand-written close
human_checks.expected: With the plugin installed, run a real Cadence dispatch, let it return, and issue NO hand-written `trace close`. `planning.mjs trace render --phase 2` shows that worker under `brackets` with a lifecycle `return` on .planning/trace.jsonl that no orchestrator step wrote.
human_checks.why_human: Out-of-reach resource, not an unexercised path: firing SubagentStop needs the host to dispatch and complete a subagent inside an installed plugin session, and this verifier has no live host session to dispatch from. Everything reachable was executed - piping a host-shaped payload into cadence-core/bin/subagent-trace.mjs against a scratch project did append the close and did move the row from unpaired to brackets - so what remains unproven is only that the host invokes the registration, which no probe in this environment can trigger.

human_checks.name: A dispatch whose close never runs is still paired
human_checks.expected: After that same live dispatch, the worker appears under `brackets` and NOT under `unpaired`, and its bracket carries identity only (no tokens, turns or duration), which is the signature of a host-written close.
human_checks.why_human: Same out-of-reach resource. The record cannot witness it yet: the hook was registered mid-run, so both of this phase's own executor brackets were closed by the hand-written path and no bracket on .planning/trace.jsonl was written by the host. Only a real dispatch after this install can produce one.
